Cache utilities

The GPCache system provides pre-allocated matrix and vector storage to avoid repeated heap allocations during message passing. This is critical for performance in large models with many observations.

GPCache

RxGPs.GPCache — Type
GPCache()

Working memory for the in-place products below: matrices and vectors keyed by a label and their size, allocated on first use and reused after. A MultiSGP rule keeps one in its scratch, which the engine holds per node.

Warning

A buffer is reused by every later call with the same label and size, so a result read from the cache stays valid only until the next such call. Copy it to keep it.

source

A GPCache holds two dictionaries, keyed by (Symbol, size) tuples:

StorageKey typeValue type
Matrices(Symbol, (nrows, ncols))Matrix{Float64}
Vectors(Symbol, length)Vector{Float64}

Create a new cache with GPCache() (all dictionaries start empty; buffers are allocated on first access).

Accessors

RxGPs.getcache — Function
getcache(cache::GPCache, label::Tuple{Symbol, Tuple{Int, Int}})
getcache(cache::GPCache, label::Tuple{Symbol, Int})

The matrix of size label[2], or the vector of length label[2], stored in cache under label, allocated (uninitialised) on first use.

source

In-place matrix operations

These functions use the cache to perform matrix multiplications without allocating intermediate arrays:

RxGPs.mul_A_B! — Function
mul_A_B!(cache::GPCache, A, B, sizeA1, sizeB2)
mul_A_B!(cache::GPCache, A, B, size1)

A * B written into a buffer of cache and returned: of size sizeA1 × sizeB2, or, for square A and B, size1 × size1. The buffer is shared with later calls of the same size (see GPCache).

source
RxGPs.mul_A_B_A! — Function
mul_A_B_A!(cache::GPCache, A, B, size1)

A * B * A for square A and B of size size1, written into a buffer of cache (see GPCache).

source
RxGPs.mul_A_B_At! — Function
mul_A_B_At!(cache::GPCache, A, B, sizeA1, sizeB1)

A * B * A' for A of size sizeA1 × sizeB1 and square B, written into a buffer of cache (see GPCache).

source
RxGPs.mul_A_v! — Function
mul_A_v!(cache::GPCache, A, v, sizeA1)

A * v written into a buffer of cache of length sizeA1 (see GPCache).

source
